explanation: Showing the sole of your foot or shoe to someone in Turkey is a real insult, especially while seated in a home, restaurant, or coffee shop — it implies the other person is beneath you. Locals avoid pointing their feet at others or propping shoes up where soles are visible.
local_tip: Keep your feet flat on the floor or crossed at the ankle, and never point the sole of your foot or shoe toward another person.
regional_note: The taboo is strongest in traditional homes and religious settings; very casual gatherings among close friends may be more relaxed.

also_check.note: The feet are the lowest and most impure part of the body; pointing them at someone or a Buddha image is a serious offense.
Showing the sole of your foot is a grave insult implying the person is beneath you.
Putting feet up or showing soles is generally casual and acceptable informally, though it can seem rude in formal settings.
